<!--

This PR allows `generic` to rewrite camera timestamps using the `use_wallclock_as_timestamps ffmpeg` option. Use of this option helps correct various issues including sporadic crashes due to packet corruption and HLS segmenting issues with audio+video streams.

Sounds good. I'll work on #71247 first. I think moving the frame rate setting to the options flow should probably just be a separate PR.
@davet2001 Maybe we should do this one before #71247 so it will be easier to cherry pick for a patch release
I see this got tagged for the milestone but isn't this a new feature to work around existing issues?

> I see this got tagged for the milestone but isn't this a new feature to work around existing issues?

Yes, I thought that since it fixed an issue it could be released as a milestone. But I assume from your comment that since it's a new feature, that it has to wait until the next version?
It's a pretty serious issue for some users, as it can cause HA to crash quite often. It hasn't affected me since I have been using the option locally since January, but my PR then was rejected as changes to yaml were forbidden. Ever since then generic has been a moving target as @davet2001 has been augmenting the config flow.
This is a new feature and should never ended up in a patch release. Even if a new feature "fixes" an issue.

issue_context.title: Home Assistant is repeatedly restarting after a critical error in the Stream component
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I am seeing random but fairly frequent restarts of Home Assistant immediately after this log entry:

`CRITICAL (stream_worker) [libav.generic] Assertion next_dts <= 0x7fffffff failed at libavformat/movenc.c:1082`

Not entirely sure when the issue started my best guess is around version 2022.2.x

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.3.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Stream

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/stream

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
CRITICAL (stream_worker) [libav.generic] Assertion next_dts <= 0x7fffffff failed at libavformat/movenc.c:1082
```


### Additional information

I have a total of 6 camera entities, 2 via the ONVIF integration, 2 via the Synology integration, 1 Ring doorbell, and a "camera" that shows the cleaning map from my Neato vacuum.  I am occasionally seeing this error in the logs also but they are more frequent then and do not seem to correlate with the restarts `ERROR (stream_worker) [homeassistant.components.stream.stream.camera.pool_camera_onvif] Error from stream worker: Timestamp overflow detected: last dts = 3993917904, dts = 44547584`

I had this iusses in summer 2021, I'm not sure of when exactly. And again since first update of home assistant in february 2022. 
I had 3 Ezviz camera with the option "preload stream" activated. 
If I deselect the option HA not restart itself. If I select the option only in 1 of the 3 camera, HA reboot itself every 26 ours and half.

apologise for my english

I am experiencing exactly the same:
home-assistant.log.1:2022-03-19 09:03:29 CRITICAL (stream_worker) [libav.generic] Assertion next_dts <= 0x7fffffff failed at libavformat/movenc.c:1082
having the same problem for a while, stream from Ezviz camera, got the error with both preload checked and unchecked
Well good news I have not had a single restart since unchecking the preload stream.  However it would be nice to be able to re-enable that feature.

Just a follow up - I added some logging and handling locally to try and work around this issue, but I haven't seen it pop up in the past week+. I'll update when I find out more.

#71245 should hopefully resolve this issue (I had hoped to merge it back in January in #64295, but there's some obsession with getting rid of configuration via yaml).

Select the "Use wallclock as timestamps" option in generic

Thank you, advanced mode is enable but I have Ezviz Camera, not a generic one so I don't have the option? I'm right?
Yes, this option is currently only available on generic. I'll reopen the issue and tag it with ONVIF and EZVIZ as it looks like those integrations need to allow the option as well.

As of 2022.6.0, the use wallclock as timestamps option is available in config options for generic and onvif as of 2022.6.0. The option will be automatically set if using the ezviz integration. Setting this option should resolve this issue.
it seems that the problem is solved, for now no reboot (3 days)!
